list.title: Clinical calculators
list.intro: Scores and formulas used in urology, each with its source. Open to everyone; what you type stays on your device and is neither sent nor saved.
list.notIncluded: IIEF, SHIM and TNM staging are not here: their owners license their use in software.

errors.notNumber: {decimals, plural, =0 {Enter a whole number.} one {Enter a number with at most # decimal.} other {Enter a number with at most # decimals.}}
errors.outOfRange: Enter a number from {min} to {max} {unit}. Outside this range the formula gives no answer.

about.disclaimer: An aid to clinical judgement, not a substitute for it. Check the result against the source before acting on it.
about.nothingStored: What you type stays on this device: nothing is sent or saved.
about.notReviewed: Not yet checked by the reviewing physician. Do not use it for patient care until it is.
about.hebrewNotValidated: The Hebrew wording of this questionnaire is ours, not a validated translation.

qol.3: Mixed: about equally satisfied and dissatisfied

location.beyond: Entirely above the upper or below the lower polar line
location.within: More than half across a polar line, crossing the axial midline, or entirely between the polar lines

ipss.name: IPSS: International Prostate Symptom Score
ipss.summary: Seven questions on urinary symptoms over the past month, and one on quality of life.

emptying.label: 1. Over the past month, how often have you had a sensation of not emptying your bladder completely after you finished urinating?

frequency.label: 2. Over the past month, how often have you had to urinate again less than two hours after you finished urinating?

intermittency.label: 3. Over the past month, how often have you found you stopped and started again several times when you urinated?

urgency.label: 4. Over the past month, how often have you found it difficult to postpone urination?

weakStream.label: 5. Over the past month, how often have you had a weak urinary stream?

straining.label: 6. Over the past month, how often have you had to push or strain to begin urination?

nocturia.label: 7. Over the past month, how many times did you most typically get up to urinate from the time you went to bed at night until the time you got up in the morning?

qol.label: Quality of life: if you were to spend the rest of your life with your urinary condition just the way it is now, how would you feel about that?

parts.qol: Quality of life (0 to 6, not added to the score)

psaDensity.name: PSA density
psaDensity.summary: Serum PSA divided by the prostate's volume.

bands.atOrAbove: 0.15 ng/mL/mL or more: at or above the cut-off most often used.

notes.volume: The density is only as good as the volume: the imaging and the way the volume is measured change the result.

psaVelocity.name: PSA velocity
psaVelocity.summary: How fast PSA rises: the change between two measurements, per year.

bands.atOrAbove: 0.75 ng/mL per year or more: the rate the source study associated with prostate cancer.

notes.short: The measurements are less than 18 months apart; over a short time, velocity is unreliable.
notes.method: Calculated from two measurements. The source used repeated measurements over years, and PSA varies between tests and laboratories.

creatinineClearance.name: Creatinine clearance (Cockcroft-Gault)
creatinineClearance.summary: Estimated creatinine clearance from age, sex, weight and serum creatinine.

notes.weight: Uses the weight as typed, as the source did. The result is in mL/min and is not adjusted to body surface area.

egfr.name: eGFR (CKD-EPI 2021)
egfr.summary: Estimated GFR from serum creatinine, age and sex, without race.

bands.g1: G1: normal or high (90 or more).
bands.g3a: G3a: mildly to moderately decreased (45 to 59).
bands.g3b: G3b: moderately to severely decreased (30 to 44).

notes.steady: Valid only when creatinine is stable, not in acute kidney injury. The categories are KDIGO's; chronic kidney disease also needs the finding to last more than 3 months.

stoneVolume.name: Stone volume
stoneVolume.summary: A stone's volume from its three diameters (as an ellipsoid), and its area on one image.

parts.area: Area on one image (π/4 × length × width)

renal.name: R.E.N.A.L. nephrometry score
renal.summary: The anatomy of a renal mass on CT or MRI, scored 4 to 12.

nearness.label: (N) Distance from the deepest part of the tumour to the collecting system or sinus

location.label: (L) Location relative to the polar lines

hilar.label: Touches the main renal artery or vein (hilar, h)

padua.name: PADUA score
padua.summary: The anatomy of a renal tumour before nephron-sparing surgery, scored 6 to 14.

collecting.label: Urinary collecting system involved (dislocated or infiltrated)

bands.low: 6 to 7: low risk of complications, in the source.
bands.intermediate: 8 to 9: intermediate risk of complications, in the source.
bands.high: 10 or more: high risk of complications, in the source.

stone.name: S.T.O.N.E. nephrolithometry
stone.summary: The complexity of kidney stones before percutaneous nephrolithotomy, from non-contrast CT.

area.label: (S) Stone size: area
area.hint: Length × width; for several stones, added together.
